title: Independent checks: agreement is not proof

sections.skill: Choose an independent check and avoid false confirmation

questions.prompt: Why is asking the same tool "Are you sure?" not an independent check?

choices.text: The tool always tells the truth when asked twice
The tool cannot answer that question
Asking twice is against the rules
It relies on the same source of possible error

questions.correct_answer: It relies on the same source of possible error
questions.intro: An INDEPENDENT CHECK is one that does not rely on the same source of possible error. Asking the same AI tool "Are you sure?" is not independent: it may simply repeat or rephrase its answer, or apologize and change a correct answer to a wrong one. Asking a second AI tool is not fully independent either, because tools trained on similar data can share the same mistakes. Agreement between them is not proof. Independent checks include the primary source, an official record, your own calculation, a measurement, or a qualified person who checks the evidence.
questions.feedback: The same source can repeat the same error.

sections.skill: Compare checking with asking a witness to vouch for himself

questions.prompt: Why does "Are you sure?" add little?

choices.text: He will always change his answer
It asks the same person again

questions.correct_answer: It asks the same person again
questions.intro: Imagine someone says he was at the library at noon. If you ask him, "Are you sure?" and he says "Yes," you have learned nothing new: it is the same person. If his twin brother says, "He was there," that sounds like confirmation, but the twin may simply repeat what he was told. An INDEPENDENT check would be the library's sign-in sheet or its camera record: evidence that does not depend on the person who made the claim.

questions.prompt: Why is the twin not a strong check?

He works at the library every day

sections.title: Apply it

sections.skill: Match the check to the claim and spot fake independence

questions.prompt: A tool wrote a function that sorts names. What is the best independent check?

choices.text: Ask the tool whether the code is correct
Run tests with known inputs and expected outputs
Ask a second tool to praise it

questions.correct_answer: Run tests with known inputs and expected outputs
questions.intro: Choosing the right independent check depends on the claim. For a fact, find the record that controls it. For a calculation, redo it. For code, run tests. For advice, ask someone accountable and qualified. Also watch for checks that only look independent: three websites copying one source, or a "review" written by the seller. If the best check is too costly, decide how much the decision matters and say honestly what remains unverified.
